primary_source.feed_identifier: NdPr Oxide 99.5% FOB China daily quote

sourcing.caveats: Chinese-dominated price discovery (~70% global supply); SMM/Asian Metal quotes are subscription-gated and reflect FOB China rather than a transparent global benchmark. REMX ETF (NYSE Arca) and MP Materials (MP) trade as listed equity proxies on Bloomberg/Refinitiv for free-tier consumers.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Dy Oxide 99.5% FOB China daily quote

sourcing.caveats: China controls ~85% of heavy REE refining; export controls (Dec 2023) added opacity. SMM/Argus/Fastmarkets quotes are paywalled FOB China. No Western terminal market exists; Lynas (LYC.AX) is the only meaningful ex-China equity proxy.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Samarium Oxide 99.9% China FOB

sourcing.caveats: Thin spot market with mostly weekly rather than daily fixings; subject to April 2025 China export controls. Prices are FOB China and paywalled; quotes can stale for weeks during quiet trade periods. No public Western proxy other than REE basket equities (REMX, LYC.AX).

primary_source.feed_identifier: LTH Lithium Hydroxide CIF CJK (Fastmarkets) futures; LIT Lithium Carbonate CIF Asia futures

sourcing.caveats: CME contracts (LTH/LIT, cash-settled vs Fastmarkets) have grown in liquidity but daily open interest remains modest vs base metals; GFEX LC contract launched Jul 2023 and is now liquid but China-domestic. Spodumene concentrate priced separately by Platts/Fastmarkets (paywalled).

primary_source.feed_identifier: LME Cobalt Cash (CO) — 99.8% min electrolytic

backup_source.feed_identifier: Cobalt sulphate 20.5% Co min, EXW China

sourcing.caveats: LME Cobalt is the global benchmark for refined metal but is illiquid (low open interest, frequent stale fixings). Battery-grade cobalt sulfate trades at a separate paywalled Fastmarkets/Argus spread; LME ≠ sulfate directly. DRC supply concentration (~70%) adds geopolitical risk.

primary_source.feed_identifier: LME Nickel Cash (LMNIDY) — Class 1 cathode/briquette

sourcing.caveats: LME Nickel suffered a credibility crisis in March 2022 (forced cancellation of trades). Class 1 vs Class 2 (NPI/MHP) basis spread is wide and paywalled (Fastmarkets). Battery-grade nickel sulfate trades at a premium separately quoted by Argus/Fastmarkets.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Manganese sulphate 32% Mn min, battery-grade, EXW China

backup_source.feed_identifier: Manganese Ore 44% CIF Tianjin (MAU) futures — bulk ore proxy only

sourcing.caveats: HPMSM (high-purity battery-grade manganese sulfate) has no terminal market; only paywalled Fastmarkets/Asian Metal weekly quote. CME MAU manganese ore futures track bulk metallurgical ore, not battery grade — basis is poor. Equity proxies: South32 (S32.AX), Eramet (ERA.PA), Element 25 (E25.AX).

primary_source.feed_identifier: Spherical Graphite 99.95% FOB China; Synthetic Graphite Anode price assessment

backup_source.feed_identifier: Flake graphite 94-97% C, -100 mesh, FOB China

sourcing.caveats: No exchange-traded futures; Benchmark and Fastmarkets are paywalled monthly assessments. China dominates synthetic anode (>95%); export controls (Dec 2023) added opacity. Equity proxies: Syrah Resources (SYR.AX), Nouveau Monde (NMG), Northern Graphite (NGC.V), POSCO Future M (003670.KS).

primary_source.feed_identifier: Ta2O5 30% min CIF China; Tantalum metal 99.95% spot

sourcing.caveats: No terminal market; opaque bilateral sales dominated by Global Advanced Metals (private), AMG, and Chinese refiners. Asian Metal/Fastmarkets quotes are paywalled and reflect Chinese spot only. ~40% of mine supply from Central Africa (DRC, Rwanda) with conflict-mineral compliance overhead.

primary_source.vendor: CBMM via shareholder filings (JFE Holdings 5411.T, ITOCHU 8001.T, CITIC 0267.HK consortium)
primary_source.feed_identifier: Annual ferro-niobium contract price disclosed in CBMM equity stakeholder reports

backup_source.feed_identifier: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries (annual) — niobium average price

sourcing.caveats: CBMM (Brazil) controls ~80% of global supply but is privately held — no spot market exists. Pricing is bilateral long-term contracts; annual USGS price is the only public benchmark. Equity proxies: 30% CBMM stake held by JFE/ITOCHU/Nippon Steel/POSCO/CITIC consortium; Niobec (Magris Resources, private); CMOC (3993.HK) for niobium-bearing byproducts.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Antimony MMTA Standard Grade II, in warehouse Rotterdam

sourcing.caveats: No exchange-traded contract. China imposed export controls Sep 2024, driving Rotterdam prices from ~$13k/t to ~$40k+/t with extreme opacity in Q4 2024-Q1 2025. Fastmarkets/Asian Metal quotes paywalled and have shown wide bid-ask. Western equity proxies are very thin: Perpetua Resources (PPTA) is pre-production; United States Antimony (UAMY) is sub-scale.

primary_source.feed_identifier: APT (Ammonium Paratungstate) 88.5% WO3 min, CIF Rotterdam

sourcing.caveats: No exchange-traded futures. APT is the industry-standard benchmark but quoted only via paywalled Fastmarkets/Argus weekly assessments. WF6 (tungsten hexafluoride for semi CVD) is a downstream specialty gas with no public price — sold via LTA. Equity proxies for tungsten: Almonty Industries (ALMTF), China Tungsten/Xiamen Tungsten (600549.SS), Sandvik (SAND.ST) for hard metal exposure.

primary_source.feed_identifier: LME Tin Cash (LMSND) — 99.85% min

sourcing.caveats: LME Tin is a transparent global benchmark with daily settled prices; spreads vs SHFE typically modest. Supply concentration risk: Indonesia (~30%), Myanmar (~12%) with periodic export halts (Wa State ban Aug 2023) causing spot volatility. Good free-tier coverage via Yahoo/Bloomberg.

primary_source.feed_identifier: LME Copper Cash (LMCADS03) — Grade A 99.99%

sourcing.caveats: Most liquid and transparent base metal market globally. LME/COMEX/SHFE all carry daily settled prices with deep open interest. Free-tier coverage excellent (Yahoo Finance HG=F, Bloomberg LMCADS03). Essentially the gold standard for live commodity pricing.

primary_source.feed_identifier: LME Aluminium Cash (LMAHDS03) — P1020A 99.7% min

sourcing.caveats: Highly liquid global benchmark with daily settled LME prices. Russian metal restrictions (April 2024 LME ban on new deliveries) created a two-tier basis but mainline LMAHDS03 remains the canonical reference. Free-tier coverage via Yahoo/Bloomberg standard.

primary_source.feed_identifier: LBMA Silver Price (12:00 London auction fix)

sourcing.caveats: LBMA fix is the global benchmark; COMEX SI futures provide continuous price discovery. Excellent free-tier coverage (XAGUSD, SI=F, SLV ETF). Industrial silver demand (solar paste, EV electronics) increasingly drives marginal price vs investment demand; small grade premiums for 4N/5N silver are paywalled.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Magnesium ingot 99.8% Pidgeon process, FOB China

sourcing.caveats: No exchange-traded futures; China supplies ~85% via paywalled Fastmarkets/Asian Metal weekly assessments. Pidgeon-process pricing dominates; Western reshoring efforts (US Magnesium UT, Latrobe Magnesium AU) are sub-scale. EU Anti-dumping duties on Chinese Mg add basis complexity. Equity proxies: US Magnesium (private), Western Magnesium (WMG.V).

primary_source.feed_identifier: Ferro-vanadium 78-82% V, in-warehouse Rotterdam; V2O5 flake 98% min China

sourcing.caveats: No terminal futures market; FeV and V2O5 are paywalled weekly assessments. Demand split between steel alloy (~90%) and vanadium redox flow batteries (~5%, growing). Equity proxies: Largo Inc (LGO), Bushveld Minerals (BMN.L, distressed), Energy Fuels (UUUU) byproduct exposure.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Yttrium Oxide 99.999% China FOB

sourcing.caveats: Heavy REE under China April 2025 export controls; ~99% of refined yttrium originates from China. Thin spot market with paywalled weekly fixings (Asian Metal/SMM). High-purity grades (99.999%, 99.9999%) for laser/phosphor use carry wide premiums not publicly published. Only equity proxy is REE basket (REMX, MP, LYC.AX) with poor specific tracking.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Bismuth 99.99%, in-warehouse Rotterdam

sourcing.caveats: No exchange-traded futures; China supplies ~80% as a byproduct of lead/tungsten/copper smelting. Fastmarkets/Asian Metal weekly quotes are paywalled. China added bismuth to export controls Feb 2025, driving sharp spot moves and widening bid-ask. No clean Western producer equity proxy at scale.

primary_source.feed_identifier: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Scandium (annual)

sourcing.caveats: Extremely thin market (~25 t/yr global consumption); no spot price feed, no exchange, no transparent benchmark. Sold via bilateral contracts between producers (Rio Tinto Sorel-Tracy, Sumitomo, NioCorp pre-production) and end-users (Airbus, Boeing for Al-Sc alloys). USGS annual figure is the only public datapoint and is often listed as range only. Equity proxies are mostly pre-production.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Terbium Oxide 99.99% FOB China

sourcing.caveats: Heavy REE under tightest China export controls (Apr 2025); ~90% of refined terbium from China. Highest unit-value REE (~$1000/kg) makes it strategically critical for NdFeB magnet heat resistance. SMM/Asian Metal daily quotes are paywalled FOB China. Only equity proxy is Lynas (LYC.AX) Mt Weld and basket ETFs (REMX); no Western terbium-specific producer at scale.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Wacker Chemie (WCH.DE) + Tokuyama (4043.T) + GCL Tech (3800.HK)

sourcing.caveats: Semi-grade (11N) polysilicon is sold via long-term contracts at 10-20x solar-grade prices; PVInsights and BNEF publish solar-grade poly prices but these are misleading for semi-grade. Best public exposure is via Wacker (largest semi-poly producer) and Tokuyama equity.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Gallium 99.99% spot (CNY/kg)

sourcing.caveats: China controls ~98% of primary gallium production and SMM is the de facto reference price; export controls since Aug 2023 have created two-tier pricing (domestic CN vs ex-China). SMM data requires subscription but is widely cited.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Indium 99.99% in-warehouse Rotterdam (USD/kg)

sourcing.caveats: Indium does not trade on LME; Fastmarkets MB and Argus publish weekly assessed prices that are reference standards. InP wafer prices are bilateral contracts (no proxy); equity exposure via Korea Zinc (010130.KS), Teck (TECK), Nyrstar.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Germanium dioxide 99.999% / Ge metal 5N spot (CNY/kg)

backup_source.feed_identifier: Argus Minor Metals — Germanium metal Rotterdam (USD/kg)

sourcing.caveats: China controls ~60% of primary supply; subject to same Aug 2023 export controls as gallium causing CN/ex-CN price divergence. SMM is the global reference but subscription-gated. USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries publishes annual lagged prices.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Tellurium ingot 99.99% spot (CNY/kg)

backup_source.feed_identifier: Argus Minor Metals — Tellurium 99.99% in-warehouse Rotterdam

sourcing.caveats: Te is a byproduct of copper refining; SMM/Argus weekly assessments are the only transparent prices. Equity exposure via 5N Plus (VNP.TO) and First Solar (FSLR) as a downstream pure-play CdTe consumer.

primary_source.feed_identifier: JM Base Prices — Ruthenium (USD/troy oz)

backup_source.feed_identifier: Heraeus PGM trading desk daily quote

sourcing.caveats: JM and Heraeus publish daily PGM base prices for Ru that are the global reference (free public access). Ru is not exchange-listed but the dealer quotes function as a fix. Highly concentrated: South Africa (Sibanye-Stillwater, Anglo American Platinum) and Russia (Norilsk) dominate supply.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Argus Minor Metals — Hafnium nuclear-grade (USD/kg)

sourcing.caveats: Hf is a byproduct of nuclear-grade Zr separation; supply is heavily constrained (Framatome/CEZUS, ATI Allegheny, China Nuclear). No exchange listing; Argus monthly assessments are reference. Equity proxy: ATI Inc. (ATI), Framatome (private, EDF parent).

primary_source.feed_identifier: Zircon sand 66% spot (CNY/t)

sourcing.caveats: Zircon sand (mineral) and Zr metal sponge have separate markets. Iluka publishes a quarterly Zircon Reference Price for mineral sand. Nuclear-grade Zr metal is bilateral. Equity proxy: Iluka (ILU.AX), Tronox (TROX), Rio Tinto Iron & Titanium.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Air Products (APD) + Linde (LIN) + Air Liquide (AI.PA)

backup_source.feed_identifier: BLM Helium In-Kind crude price (legacy, BLM auction wound down 2024)

sourcing.caveats: Helium is sold via 5-10 year take-or-pay contracts, not a spot market. BLM Cliffside auction ended; remaining published prices (e.g. Gasworld 'Helium Shortage 4.0' commentary) are commentary, not transparent feed. Equity exposure via the industrial-gas majors is the only public price discovery.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Industry commentary on contract prices (USD/m3)

backup_source.feed_identifier: Equity proxy for ex-Ukraine neon supply

sourcing.caveats: Litho-grade neon is sold via LTAs to ~10 customers globally (TSMC, Samsung, Intel, etc.). The Russia/Ukraine war caused price spikes from ~$350/m3 to >$2,500/m3 in 2022 but those are commentary numbers, not exchange-settled. No publicly available daily feed.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Industry commentary on contract prices (USD/m3)

backup_source.feed_identifier: Equity proxy via industrial gas majors

sourcing.caveats: Xenon is extracted from air separation units at scale of ~70 m3/day globally; sold by ASU operators under bilateral contracts. No transparent daily price. Spot quotes from Edelhoff and similar German distributors are the only published reference, available via Gasworld/CryoGas commentary.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Industry commentary on contract prices (USD/m3)

backup_source.feed_identifier: Equity proxy via industrial gas majors

sourcing.caveats: Krypton is co-produced with xenon from air separation; same opaque market structure with ~6-8 global producers and LTA contracts. Russia/Ukraine war impacted supply (Iceblick, Cryoin); spot price discovery via Gasworld commentary only.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Linde (LIN) + Air Liquide (AI.PA) + Air Products (APD)

sourcing.caveats: Argon is ~1% of atmospheric air, abundant and cheap; electronic-grade (6N/9N) is a small premium over bulk industrial argon. No commodity exchange listing. Industrial-gas majors capture margin from purification rather than the gas itself. CRU bulk-gas price reports exist behind subscription.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Resonac (4004.T) + Kanto Denka (4047.T) + SK Specialty (private; ex-036490.KQ delisted Dec-2021)

backup_source.feed_identifier: Tungsten APT 88.5% (USD/mtu) as upstream input proxy

sourcing.caveats: WF6 is a specialty electronic gas sold via LTAs to fabs; no spot market. Tungsten APT price (LME 2024 launched contract LMTPL; SMM and Argus assessments) tracks upstream metal input but not WF6 purification premium. Equity proxy via Resonac, Kanto Denka, and SK Materials is the most direct.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Linde (LIN) + REC Silicon (RECSI legacy) + Air Liquide (AI.PA) + Mitsui Chemicals (4183.T)

sourcing.caveats: Silane is produced captively by polysilicon makers (REC Silicon, Wacker) and electronic-gas majors. Disilane is a niche product (~$5,000+/kg) sold under fab LTAs. No public spot price; equity proxy via the gas/poly producers is the only path.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Argus FMB Ammonia FOB Tampa / CFR NW Europe (weekly USD/t)

backup_source.feed_identifier: CME Tampa Ammonia futures (low liquidity, contract code NH3)

sourcing.caveats: Bulk anhydrous ammonia has transparent weekly benchmarks (Tampa, Yuzhnyy, NW Europe). Electronic-grade (8N/9N purified) carries a 50-200x premium for fab-grade and is sold under bilateral LTAs by Resonac, Taiyo Nippon Sanso (4091.T), Air Liquide. The bulk price is a directional but not equivalent proxy.

primary_source.feed_identifier: SK Specialty (private; ex-036490.KQ delisted Dec-2021) + Kanto Denka (4047.T) + Hyosung Chemical (298000.KS) + Foosung (093370.KS)

sourcing.caveats: NF3 is ~80% controlled by Korean producers (SK Specialty, Hyosung, Foosung) plus Japan (Kanto Denka, Showa Denko/Resonac). Sold via fab LTAs at $25-50/kg; no spot market. Equity proxy via the four primary producers is the most direct exposure.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Acidspar (97% CaF2) FOB China (USD/t) — upstream fluorspar feedstock

sourcing.caveats: Fluorspar is the upstream input with transparent Argus/IM weekly assessments; bulk HF has IHS Markit assessments. Electronic-grade anhydrous HF carries 10-50x premium and is sold under LTAs by Stella Chemifa, Morita Chemical, Soulbrain, Do-Fluoride. Korean HF was the 2019 Japan-export-control flashpoint.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Wolfspeed (WOLF) + Coherent (COHR) + SiCrystal-Resonac (4004.T) + SICC (688234.SS) + TanKeBlue (688275.SS)

sourcing.caveats: 150mm and 200mm SiC wafer ASPs are tracked by Yole, TrendForce, and Omdia (subscription); no public daily feed. Wolfspeed is the most-traded pure-play; SICC and TanKeBlue (CN) are listed but newer. Strong equity proxy because wafer revenue ~= ASP x volume disclosed in quarterly reports. NOTE: Wolfspeed entered Chapter 11 reorganization in 2025 — pre-/post-reorg price series are discontinuous and must not be spliced.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Sumitomo Electric (5802.T) + Mitsubishi Chemical (4188.T) + Soitec (SOI.PA) + Sumco (3436.T) GaN-on-Si effort

sourcing.caveats: Bulk GaN substrate market is small (~$200M/yr) and dominated by Sumitomo Electric and Mitsubishi Chemical (private GaN subsidiary). GaN-on-SiC and GaN-on-Si epi wafers from Soitec and Sumco. No transparent price; equity proxy is partial since GaN is small revenue share at each producer.

primary_source.feed_identifier: JSR (4185.T, delisted 2024 to JIC) + Tokyo Ohka Kogyo (4186.T) + Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T) + Sumitomo Chemical (4005.T) + Fujifilm (4901.T)

sourcing.caveats: EUV resist is a ~$1.5B/yr oligopoly (JSR via JIC takeover, TOK, Shin-Etsu, Sumitomo, Fujifilm); ArF immersion adds Inpria (acquired by JSR). Sold under fab LTAs with strict NDA pricing. JSR delisting in 2024 reduces public exposure; TOK (4186.T) and Shin-Etsu remain best public proxies.

primary_source.feed_identifier: CMC Materials (acquired by Entegris ENTG 2022) + Fujimi (5384.T) + Resonac (4004.T) + Versum-Merck (MRK.DE) + KCTech (281820.KS) + Soulbrain (357780.KQ)

sourcing.caveats: CMP slurry market is ~$2.5B/yr; CMC Materials was the pure-play and was acquired by Entegris (ENTG) in 2022, reducing pure-play exposure. Sold under fab LTAs. Equity proxy via Entegris (now diversified), Fujimi, Resonac, and Merck KGaA covers the global supply.

sourcing.commodity: Sputtering targets (Ta, Ti, Cu, Co, Ru)

primary_source.feed_identifier: JX Advanced Metals (5020.T, IPO'd TSE Mar-2025, ENEOS retains ~42%) + Materion (MTRN) + Honeywell Electronic Materials (HON) + Plansee Group (private) + Solar Applied Materials (3674.TWO)

backup_source.feed_identifier: LME Cu/Ni/Co + JM Ru/Ta base prices (upstream metal feedstock)

sourcing.caveats: Sputtering target market is consolidated: JX Advanced Metals (~60% share; IPO'd TSE Mar-2025), Materion, Honeywell, Plansee, ULVAC. Targets carry 5-20x premium over raw metal due to high-purity sintering. Upstream metals (Cu LMCADS03, Ru JM, Co LMCO, Ta MB) provide directional baseline.

sourcing.commodity: Synthetic fused silica / EUV mask blanks

primary_source.feed_identifier: Hoya (7741.T) + Shin-Etsu Chemical (4063.T) + AGC (5201.T) + Tosoh (4042.T)

backup_source.feed_identifier: Corning Display Tech segment (synthetic fused silica reporting unit)

sourcing.caveats: EUV mask blank market is a duopoly: Hoya (~70%) and AGC (~30%) for EUV; Shin-Etsu and Tosoh strong in 193nm/ArF. Mask blanks sell at ~$30K each; fused silica boule is intermediate. Sold under multi-year supply agreements with ASML mask shop ecosystem. Strong equity proxy because the producer set is small and concentrated.

primary_source.feed_identifier: PA= / PAL (NYMEX Palladium Futures, front-month)

sourcing.caveats: Highly liquid PGM with transparent settled prices on NYMEX and LBMA fix. Pricing is for refined palladium sponge/ingot; rocket-grade catalytic applications follow spot with minor processing premium.

primary_source.feed_identifier: UX (UxC U3O8 Futures, front-month) — settled against UxC Broker Average Price

backup_source.feed_identifier: UxC Weekly Spot U3O8 Price Indicator / TradeTech Weekly U3O8 Spot Price

sourcing.caveats: Spot uranium is thinly traded (~15-20% of volume); 80%+ moves via long-term utility contracts. UxC and TradeTech weekly indicators are paywalled but NYMEX UX futures provide daily transparent settlement reference.

primary_source.feed_identifier: NG= / NGc1 (Henry Hub Natural Gas Futures, front-month)

sourcing.caveats: Henry Hub itself is the most liquid global gas benchmark with full daily settlement. However, as a methalox propellant proxy, the basis to rocket-grade LNG/CH4 (purity 99.9%+, cryogenic processing, transport) adds a substantial cost layer not captured by Henry Hub.

primary_source.feed_identifier: LIN (Linde plc), APD (Air Products), AI.PA (Air Liquide), 4091.T (Nippon Sanso)

backup_source.feed_identifier: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Industrial Gases (annual)

sourcing.caveats: LOX is sold under multi-year bilateral supply contracts between industrial gas majors and end-users (SpaceX, ULA, Blue Origin). No public spot or futures market exists. Pricing tracked indirectly through Linde / Air Products / Air Liquide equity earnings disclosures and segment margins.

primary_source.feed_identifier: Argus Hydrazine Hydrate Monthly / Tecnon OrbiChem Chem-Net (subscription only)

sourcing.caveats: MMH and UDMH (rocket-grade) sold almost exclusively via cost-plus government and aerospace contracts (Arianespace, Roscosmos, US DoD); no public spot price. Hydrazine hydrate (industrial precursor) has paywalled Argus/Tecnon prints but rocket-grade derivatives are bilateral.

primary_source.feed_identifier: TKA.DE (thyssenkrupp Uhde — N2O4 plant licensor), 600291.SS (Sinochem), aerospace contractor disclosures

sourcing.caveats: N2O4 / MON-3 / MON-25 sold to satellite operators and launch providers via long-term allocation contracts with state-aligned chemical producers. No public spot or proxy market; equity exposure is indirect through diversified specialty chemical and nitric acid producers. Industrial nitric acid (precursor) has Argus prints but the bridge to MON-grade is opaque.

primary_source.feed_identifier: HO= (NY Harbor ULSD/Heating Oil Futures, front-month) or Jet-A Platts USGC

backup_source.feed_identifier: Platts Jet Fuel USGC / Argus Kerosene Type A1 (subscription)

sourcing.caveats: RP-1 is a highly refined narrow-cut kerosene (MIL-DTL-25576) sold under sole-source contracts (SpaceX, ULA, RocketLab via specialist refiners like Calumet). Heating oil / Jet-A futures provide a directional basis but RP-1 carries a 3-5x premium for olefin-free, sulfur-stripped specification. Basis adjustment is opaque.

primary_source.feed_identifier: LIN (Linde), APD (Air Products), AI.PA (Air Liquide), PLUG (Plug Power), 4091.T (Nippon Sanso)

backup_source.feed_identifier: DOE Hydrogen Shot / IEA Global Hydrogen Review (annual cost tracking)

sourcing.caveats: LH2 (cryogenic, 20K, 99.9999% purity) sold via bilateral long-term contracts to NASA/SpaceX/Blue Origin and industrial users. No public spot market; cost tracked via industrial gas major equity disclosures and DOE/IEA periodic cost reports. Gaseous H2 has emerging hub indexes but LH2 carries 2-3x liquefaction premium.

primary_source.feed_identifier: DOE NIDC (National Isotope Development Center) periodic price lists / GAO Helium-3 Reports

sourcing.caveats: He-3 is allocation-based via the DOE Isotope Program and US Tritium decay stockpile. No public market; quoted in occasional GAO reports and DOE solicitations at ~$3000-$5000/L STP. Emerging private suppliers (Pacific Fusion, Helion offtake) are pre-commercial. Cartel-like state-controlled distribution.

primary_source.feed_identifier: HRC= (US Midwest Domestic Hot-Rolled Coil Steel Futures, front-month)

backup_source.feed_identifier: CLF (Cleveland-Cliffs — sole US GOES producer), 5401.T (Nippon Steel), POSCO (005490.KS), TKA.DE (thyssenkrupp)

sourcing.caveats: GOES is a premium specialty grade with no direct futures market. HRC futures provide directional carbon-steel basis but GOES carries a 4-8x premium for high-permeability silicon alloy processing. Trade-protected (AD/CVD duties in US/EU). Cleveland-Cliffs (CLF) is the sole US producer — equity is the cleanest exposure.
